requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.python.fingerprints`. I did not read the implementation.

**Ordinary comments excluded.**
- `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has a Python case. Own-line and trailing comments are changed or removed, and the `def[f]` hash is asserted equal. A changed non-comment word (`x` to `y`) is asserted to give a different hash.
- `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` has a Python case with an edited comment. Its hash is asserted equal to the original.

**Whitespace-separated words, with each word encoded separately.**
- The same `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` Python case asserts that `"two words"` and `"two   words"` hash equal.
- It also asserts that `"two words"` and `"twowords"` differ.

**SHA-256 digest.**
- The Python case in `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` asserts a 64-character hex value.
- The shared encoder is checked against standard SHA-256 vectors in `fn[hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests]`. That test is not marked for the Python requirement, but the encoder is common to all languages.
- The Python-specific test therefore only proves a 256-bit hex form. I judge that adequate here because the algorithm sits in the shared encoder, which has its own known-answer test.

**Fingerprint scheme.**
- `tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` asserts `languages::Python` reports `python-structural-v1`.
- The same test asserts that `OutlineContent` retains that scheme (`inferred.fingerprint_scheme()` equals the language's scheme) for a `.PYI` file.

**Docstrings participate in hashes.**
- In `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries`, a docstring `"""two words"""` changed to `"changed words"` changes the `def[f]` fingerprint.
- Whitespace-only reflow of the docstring leaves the fingerprint unchanged.
- This shows the docstring is hashed as words, not excluded as a comment.
- The other expressions (`return 1`) are covered by the comment-exclusion case that changes `return x` to `return y`.

**Definition's other expressions.**
- `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[python_decorators_attach_to_the_decorated_definition_for_hashing]` checks decorator changes and removal, and that blank-line and indentation changes leave the hash equal.
- It also checks that a method's decorator changes the class's structural hash but not its identity hash.

I found no gap, and no acknowledgments apply.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Ordinary comments are excluded. Docstrings are source expressions and
participate in hashes along with the definition's other expressions.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
